# MCP server development guide — agent-centric tool design

Selected by Skill Harbor — short listing (the repo states no license — its terms live in a LICENSE.txt the manifest could not confirm, so no content is reproduced): @composiohq's mcp-builder skill — the guide for creating high-quality MCP servers in Python (FastMCP) or Node/TypeScript (MCP SDK). Phase 1: deep research and planning — agent-centric design principles (build for workflows not API endpoints, optimize for limited context, actionable error messages, natural task subdivisions, evaluation-driven development), study the MCP protocol and SDK docs, exhaustively study the target API's docs, then write an implementation plan (tool selection, shared utilities, input/output design, error-handling strategy). Phase 2: implementation — project setup, core infrastructure first, systematic tool implementation (Pydantic/Zod input schemas, comprehensive docstrings, tool annotations like readOnlyHint/idempotentHint), language-specific best practices. Phase 3: review and refine — DRY/composability/consistency/type-safety review, safe testing (never run the server in the main process), quality checklists. Phase 4: evaluations — 10 complex, realistic, read-only, verifiable evaluation questions in a prescribed XML format. Honest caveats: guidance only — the agent must already run Claude Code and needs a service API to integrate; similar concept to the existing `anthropics-mcp-builder` listing (different author, different content — not a duplicate); license terms live in the repo's...
